governing_spec.section: U3 — Command Admission／Confirmation／Audit 一次收斂 (residual defect from BFF-TEST-MIGRATION-B05)

layer_1_router_binding.defect: submit_action was bound to a lambda with 6 positional parameters named (entity_type, entity_id, action_id, resolved_key, identity, payload), but GovernanceService.submit_governance_action (governance/service.py:1241) always calls self.submit_action(action_kind=..., target_id=..., action_id=..., payload=..., identity=..., idempotency_key=...) — none of those keyword names match the lambda's positional parameter names, so every call raised TypeError: <lambda>() got an unexpected keyword argument 'action_kind'.
layer_1_router_binding.reproduction: python3 -c invocation of the pre-fix lambda body with the exact keyword call governance/service.py makes reproduces: TypeError: broken() got an unexpected keyword argument 'action_kind' (captured verbatim during this task's verification; see verification.pre_fix_typeerror_repro below).

layer_2_missing_command_type.defect: _gov_bff_action_command requires 7 parameters including command_type: CommandType. The broken lambda only forwarded 6 args and never supplied command_type, so even a keyword-name fix alone would still raise TypeError: missing 1 required positional argument: 'command_type'.
layer_2_missing_command_type.note: _gov_bff_action_command itself was NOT broken and was left unmodified — incidents/router.py's bff_risk_alert_action and bff_incident_action call it correctly today with all 7 positional args (ObjectType.RISK_ALERT/INCIDENT, id, action_id, resolved_key, identity, payload, CommandType.RISK_ALERT_ACTION/INCIDENT_ACTION). Only the governance composition-root binding was defective.

layer_3_no_product_owner_for_mapping.defect: The action_kind/action_id -> ObjectType/CommandType mapping, and a full concurrency-safe command-admission implementation, existed only inside the test file's test-local FastAPI app (_build_app), never in product code. Product traffic through bff_main.app had no working implementation of this mapping at all.

single_owner_of_mapping.location: services/control-plane/bff/command_adapters/service.py: module-level _GOVERNANCE_ACTION_KIND_OBJECT_TYPES / _GOVERNANCE_DECISION_COMMAND_TYPES tables plus resolve_governance_object_type()/resolve_governance_command_type() helpers, consumed exclusively by CommandAdapterService.submit_governance_action.

mapping.action_kind=approval, other action_id (e: ObjectType.APPROVAL_DECISION, command_type=CommandType.REQUEST_APPROVAL_REVISION (pass-through pending a dedicated command type, matching the removed test-local fallback)

command_adapter_service_owns_the_path.implementation: Owns body-idempotency-key rejection, request-hash based idempotency replay/conflict (self._gov_bff_idempotency, the same dict instance the pre-existing incidents/risk-alert path already shared via _GOV_BFF_IDEMPOTENCY), dry-run short-circuit, staleness-warning projection, and CommandStore admission + CommandResponse projection (project_final_command_response). Approval decisions use CommandStore.submit_command_if_no_active_target (concurrency-safe: a second conflicting decision on the same approval_id while the first is still in flight gets 409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT/concurrent_safety, matching the pre-existing decide-conflict contract tests). Review actions use plain CommandStore.submit_command (no active-target guard), because a review legitimately receives a sequential submit-then-act command pair on the same target with nothing in this seam marking the first command terminal; gating that pair would break the two-call POST /bff/reviews -> POST /bff/reviews/{id}/actions/{id} workflow that the ordered acceptance criteria requires.

main_py_thin_binding.before: submit_action=lambda entity_type, entity_id, action_id, resolved_key, identity, payload: _gov_bff_action_command(entity_type, entity_id, action_id, resolved_key, identity, payload)
main_py_thin_binding.note: main.py now holds zero mapping/normalization logic for this path; the binding is a direct method reference to the CommandAdapterService instance already constructed at main.py:6619 (command_adapter_service = _CommandAdapterService(...), which already shared gov_bff_idempotency=_GOV_BFF_IDEMPOTENCY with the untouched incidents-router path).

typed_submit_action_protocol.after: class SubmitAction(Protocol): def __call__(self, *, action_kind: str, target_id: str, action_id: str, payload: Mapping[str, Any], identity: Any, idempotency_key: str) -> Union[Any, Awaitable[Any]]: ...
typed_submit_action_protocol.static_check_evidence: The pre-fix lambda's positional-parameter signature (entity_type, entity_id, action_id, resolved_key, identity, payload) is structurally incompatible with the keyword-only SubmitAction Protocol (would fail assignment under a Protocol-aware type checker); a project-wide mypy run was not available as a governed check for this package layout (services/control-plane maps to services.control_plane via sys.path, not a mypy-configured path — no mypy.ini/pyproject mypy section exists for this service and no CI job type-checks it), so the primary evidence for this criterion is the runtime TypeError reproduction below plus the new regression suite exercising the real composition-root binding end to end.

batch_decide_body_idempotency_key_owned_.location: services/control-plane/bff/governance/router.py: create_governance_router(reject_body_idempotency_key=...) + bff_approvals_batch_decide calls _reject_body_idempotency_key(payload) on the outer batch payload before iterating decisions.
batch_decide_body_idempotency_key_owned_.wiring: services/control-plane/bff/main.py: create_governance_router(..., reject_body_idempotency_key=_reject_body_idempotency_key) uses the same product-owned function main.py already uses for every other final-contract route.

removed_test_local_seam.replaced_with: Real composition root: services.control_plane.bff.main.app via fastapi.testclient.TestClient, with the module-global bff_main.command_store swapped to a private on-disk CommandStore per test, and bff_main.app_deps.read_surface.get_approval_decision/list_approval_decisions/dataset_source patched to serve the same two approval fixtures (appr-dec-c5a9f11e pending, approval-042 decided) the removed test-local ReadPorts class used to serve. The governance router captures app_deps.read_surface as a fixed object reference at import time (not a re-resolved lookup), so those three methods are patched directly on that instance rather than swapping a module-global name.
